decisionMemo.businessProblem: A Series B analytics/BI SaaS has seen implementation time-to-go-live more than double (8→19 weeks), forming a 28-customer backlog, with the 9-person services team booked 14 weeks out. The owner suspects a time-to-value/customer-success problem and considers broad CS investment or product changes. But the product is well-regarded post-go-live (CSAT 8.4, post-go-live NPS 52, NRR 102%); dissatisfaction is concentrated specifically in the waiting/implementation phase (implementation NPS 18). Sales bookings are up 40% and new starts outpace go-lives by ~3 per month, widening the backlog, while ~60% of implementation hours sit in partly-manual data-modeling and connector setup. This is a throughput/capacity bottleneck in a specialized delivery function, compounded by manual steps, that delays revenue recognition and expansion (both wait on go-live) by nearly five months. With 22 months of runway and a board demanding efficient growth, the owner must decide whether to keep selling at pace (worsening the backlog), add services capacity, or automate the bottleneck steps.
